correctness.rationale: For agent i with a own and b other iid Bernoulli(p_i) goods, realized EF1 is precisely Y_i<=X_i+1 where X_i~Bin(a,p_i), Y_i~Bin(b,p_i); independent agents make both fairness probabilities multiply. At m=4, direct binomial expansions yield f(p_1)f(p_2) for 2:2 and g(p_singleton) for 1:3. Any 0:4 is strictly improved by moving one good. Since g strictly decreases on (0,1), singleton goes to the lower p. Rearranging g(s)>f(s)f(t) yields t^2(1-t)^2>H(s), with strictly increasing H, unique quartic threshold s_c≈0.2032804404095 and symmetric nonmonotone t interval. For fixed m with p_i=eps*lambda_i, violation first requires two other-valued goods, giving quadratic loss lambda1² C(m-a,2)+lambda2² C(a,2)+O(eps), uniformly over finite a choices; its discrete consecutive difference proves the unique/two-candidate optimizer rule. Independently checked exact rational four-good gap 7902186119/10^12, threshold, polynomial factoring. Finite checks corroborate rather than replace exact binomial argument.
residual_risks: No claim for dependent values, more agents, non-binary goods, or m growing with eps^-1. At integer theta ties, finite-eps preference deliberately not determined.

evidence: Igarashi-Oh title/abstract describes exact EF under convolution-type marginal laws, not a readable assertion of this exact EF1 curve. broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither a stronger exact-EF theorem nor a shared-realization EF1 balancing theorem dominates independent agent-specific EF1 probability optimization. Lack of access to full Igarashi-Oh is explicitly carried as priority risk.

evidence: Shared-realization Bernoulli EF1 balancing is not applicable when every agent independently samples value of the same good. The sister four-good counterexample allows p_j to vary by good but equal across agents; current claim lets p_i vary by agent but constant across goods, so neither one is a corollary of the other without additional identities.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The two parameter axes do not contain one another. Only overlapping motivation (four-good possibility) is prior, while exact phase and all-fixed-m quadratic-rate classification are distinct.

evidence: This claim uses independent realization for each agent-good and a constant Bernoulli probability within each agent; EF1 event each ordered agent X+1>=Y. A published shared-Bernoulli model uses one common realized item value across agents, so its balancing theorem has different coupling.
